findings.title: Migration crashes when no category matches the old embed_category setting
findings.body: The category lookup dereferences `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking whether the query returned a row. `embed_category` defaults to an empty value and may also name a deleted/nonexistent category, so a normal installation with no configured embedding category produces an empty result and raises on `nil['id']`. This prevents the entire database migration from completing; handle an empty result and fall back to the uncategorized category before dereferencing it.

findings.title: Migrated URL-form host entries no longer match embedding requests
findings.body: The migration inserts legacy host-list values directly into the new table, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. Existing supported values such as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` are therefore stored with their scheme/path, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` extracts only `example.com` and queries for an exact stored host. After upgrade those migrated hosts are never allowed, disabling embeds for affected sites. Normalize each legacy value to its hostname before insertion (and avoid raw SQL interpolation).

findings.title: Hosts configured with a port can never be allowed
findings.body: The validation explicitly permits values such as `example.com:3000`, and the callback leaves the port intact because it only removes schemes and paths. However `URI(host).host` drops the port before the exact database lookup, so a request from `http://example.com:3000` searches for `example.com` and cannot match the stored `example.com:3000`. Either normalize stored values to hostname-only or consistently include and compare the port.

findings.title: Deleting all allowed hosts no longer disables expansion of embedded posts
findings.body: This removes the only check that embedding is configured without replacing it with `EmbeddableHost.exists?`. Consequently, if `embed_truncate` is enabled, any existing `TopicEmbed` remains expandable even after every allowed host has been removed. Host removal should disable embedding behavior; otherwise stale embed records can still expose the expansion UI and trigger remote content retrieval.
